EPA 82 gal/day claim is accurate. #6 water reconnection fee range '$25-$150' is UNVERIFIED (no supporting citation). #6 tariff references (PG&E Rule 23 etc.) are internal document names, not browsable URLs — NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW.

PAGE #6 — LIHEAP claim (6.7 million households in 2024) is ACCURATE. liheap.org (retrieved 2026-08-29) states the program 'provides heating and cooling assistance to roughly 6.7 million households.'
PAGE #6 — DOE source (energy.gov/save/home-upgrades) is a generic top-level page, not a reconnection-fee policy page. The source does not specifically support the reconnection-fee content.

PAGE #6 — Water reconnection fee range '$25-$150' is stated without a supporting citation. The three cited sources (CFPB, LIHEAP, DOE) do not contain water reconnection fee data. This is an UNVERIFIED claim.

PAGE #7 — Leak indicator content is factually accurate and well-structured. EPA WaterSense leak detection page (retrieved 2026-08-29) confirms guidance about detecting leaks via flow monitoring devices. 67% bounce is the best of the 4 pages.

PAGE #7 — Trailing-slash split (68/27): the site has .htaccess 301 redirect rules in static/.htaccess lines 49-50. The canonical tag uses .Permalink (no frontmatter override). The 27 non-slash visits are likely Rybbit recording the pre-redirect URL. This is normal behavior — no fix needed, but monitor GSC for non-canonical indexing.

PAGE #8 — 93.8% bounce on 85pv is a critical defect. Three root causes: (1) INTENT MISMATCH — page title is 'How to Investigate a Higher-Than-Expected Water Bill' but dominant search intent for 'water bill too high' is 'tell me the most common causes ranked by likelihood'. The page leads with a procedure instead of a diagnosis. (2) THIN CONTENT — only 1,094 words of body text, shorter than #23 (1,887 words). (3) PRODUCT BOXES UPFRONT — two product boxes (Govee leak detectors, Moen Flo) appear mid-page as the most visually prominent elements, signaling commercial intent to a reader who wants information.

PAGE #8 — CONFIRMED overlap with #23 (why-did-my-water-bill-suddenly-increase): #23 has 77.8% br (better) with 1,887 words and a 'most common reasons' structure. #8 has 1,094 words with a procedural structure. #8 outranks #23 (85pv vs 27pv) for the 'why spike?' query despite having worse content — cannibalization risk.
PAGE #8 — '82 gallons per day' claim from EPA WaterSense is ACCURATE. EPA page (retrieved 2026-08-29) states 'Each American uses an average of 82 gallons of water a day at home (USGS, 2015).'
SITE-WIDE — None of the 4 pages have an explicit 'canonical' frontmatter parameter. Hugo's .Permalink is used as canonical, which outputs the trailing-slash version. This is correct.
